explanation: To "contract" a habit means to acquire or develop it, the same way someone contracts an illness. Mr. Brooke picked up a rambling habit of mind during his travels, so "developed" fits. "Restricted" is the tempting choice because contract can mean shrink, but a habit that makes his conclusions unpredictable was gained, not narrowed.

Because much of the evidence about Hatshepsut's reign was destroyed, we will probably never have a complete, thorough account of it, so "exhaustive" is the logical word. "Superficial" fails because a shallow account is exactly what limited evidence would allow; the text is saying a full account is unlikely.

The underlined portion explains how adding glycerol lets a bubble pull water from the air and offset evaporation, which is one way the researchers made bubbles last much longer. That is the effect of a researcher-devised process that increases the bubble's longevity. Choice C fails because the portion shows how evaporation can be counteracted, not why it must inevitably happen.

The text contrasts a field dominated by white male authors with Butler's success breaking into it and winning major awards. So she did not see the genre as impossible to enter, or "impenetrable." "Legitimate" or "compelling" would make little sense, since her eager participation shows she did value the genre.

The last sentence explains that the nose is delicate and sticks out, making it especially easy to break. That describes something "fragile." "Recognizable" may be true of noses but does not explain why noses are the part that goes missing.

Text 2 says the possibility of nanohybrids being more toxic than their parts "has drawn deserved attention," agreeing it is a real concern, but then notes that the effects "vary by case" and gives an example where conjugation actually reduced harm. That matches D. Choice A fails because Text 2 never claims benefits outweigh the risk; it only shows that the risky outcome is not guaranteed.

The speaker asks the waves to rock him to sleep and let him drift away from "toil and care" toward a "peaceful" place with a "soothing" lullaby. The poem expresses a longing for the ocean to bring him calm. Choice B is tempting, but the poem barely describes everyday life; it focuses on the desired peace rather than a contrast.

The text names al-Idrisi's collection of maps, explains its title, and describes how he made it by consulting older maps and interviewing travelers. So it describes a collection of medieval maps and how it was created. Choice D fails because Arabic and Greek maps are only mentioned as sources, not compared.

The text first explains how López-Morales's team used the JWST to detect carbon dioxide on WASP-39b, then says why the finding matters: it is the first decisive evidence of CO₂ on an exoplanet and shows the telescope's potential. That is a discovery followed by its importance. No alternative method, hypothesis, or challenge is mentioned, so A, C, and D fail.

The second sentence says the algae reabsorb carbon dioxide they produce and use it again for photosynthesis, which is "reuse" of carbon. Some reuse was expected, but not this much. "Supply" does not capture the idea of using the same carbon a second time.

The underlined portion tells us what scientists believed before the discovery (Denisovans lived only in cold, high places). That background makes clear why finding a tooth in warm, low-altitude Laos is significant. Choice A fails because it does not dismiss the research; the new research actually revises the older belief.

The underlined portion notes that the motif was repeated during a period of drought and population decline. The next sentence uses that fact to interpret the motif as a way of preserving cultural knowledge during stress, so the portion is a consideration behind that interpretation. Choice C fails because the text never says the motif abruptly stopped being made.

Just before the underlined portion, the text claims that higher production quotas gave employees more bargaining power. The underlined part spells out how that worked: workers demanded better benefits and anxious employers agreed. So it elaborates on an earlier claim about labor relations in the food processing industry. Choice D fails because it adds no new details about who the workers were.

Jane goes about her work "tranquilly," yet her mind keeps filling with thoughts of leaving Thornfield and finding a new job. The text contrasts her calm outward behavior with her inner restlessness. Choice D overstates things: she is only idly imagining new positions, not determined to secure one.

Video cameras had just become affordable, giving artists capabilities that were "previously unavailable," so their access to the technology was "newfound." "Inevitable" and "habitual" do not fit access that was brand new.

Seira et al. found that risk-disclosure messages had only small, short-lived effects, but they still said such effects may be worth pursuing because messaging costs almost nothing. The underlined phrase is the reason they did not dismiss messaging altogether. Choice C gets the cost relationship backward: the cost is negligible, so the small effects are not small relative to it.

Text 1 says Wright blames Neolithic pastoralists' livestock for drying out the Sahara. Brierley's team found that the humid period ended 500 years earlier than assumed, which suggests the herders did not cause the aridity and may even have delayed it. So Brierley would argue that, given the new timeline, pastoralism likely did not cause desertification. Choice B fails because Text 2 rejects the idea that pastoralism contributed at all.

The first sentence explains what yawn contagion is, and the rest of the text discusses research on that behavior in wild gelada monkeys. So it defines a phenomenon discussed in the text. It is not a problem, a challenged claim, or a hypothesis.

In the study, cuttlefish routinely showed restraint by waiting for a favorite treat, which means they are capable, or "competent," at self-control. "Awkward" would mean the opposite, and "manageable" describes something being controlled, not a skill.

The text says location choices are not purely economic but are also influenced by noneconomic factors like social networks. "Mediated by" means shaped or influenced by, so it fits. "Decoupled from" would say the choices are unconnected to those factors, the opposite of the intended point.

Ishii and O'Mahony used mushroom and kombu broths to define the pure umami taste, and judges agreed on that taste. Jünger et al. found that certain dipeptides boost umami but also add saltiness. A broth meant to represent pure umami probably lacked much of these dipeptides, since they would have added a salty taste. Choice C goes beyond both texts: neither says fermentation is what introduces these proteins.

A huge cast, a wandering plot, and backward page numbers all make the novel intricate, so a short review cannot capture its "complexity." "Accuracy" and "restraint" do not match these features at all.

The savant judges a fashionable man at a party to be a silly fop, is surprised by his good sense, and then learns he is the famous scientist Humphry Davy. The passage tells the story of a mistaken judgment, a misunderstanding. Choice D fails because the text shows why the savant was wrong about Davy, not a lasting dislike.

Text 1 says Ailey's love of jazz shows in the music he chose, and Text 2 says jazz shows in his improvisational choreography. Both agree jazz strongly influenced his work. Choice A is only touched on in Text 2, and C and D are not supported by either text.

The underlined items list the different catches the waters sometimes give: black pomfrets this time, but at other times only prawns or squid, or unusual colorful fish. Together they show how "temperamental" and unpredictable the fishing grounds are. Choice C fails because only pomfrets were caught on this trip.
Diversification protects investors from big losses, so it is considered wise and careful, or "prudent." "Contentious" and "unworkable" contradict the benefit the text describes.

Fierer's team says the environment "severely restricts" microbial survival, and Text 2 says the very low numbers of microbes would show how challenging the conditions are. Both agree that most microbes cannot survive in that soil. Choice B fails because neither text suggests a new sample would find many more microbes.
Cities are described as "seductive" and "charming," so "beckoning" means attractive and appealing, or "inviting." "Signaling" is too literal; the cities are not making a gesture.

Text 1 says scholars read facial markings on the vessels as real scars and skin conditions. Trever argues that the vessels are creative artworks inspired by real people but exploring abstract ideas, so she would say the markings are not necessarily realistic details of specific individuals. Choice B fails because she questions treating the vessels as portraits of identifiable people.

Making more than 250,000 hand-cut images over three years and inventing new tools describes a difficult, demanding process, which is "arduous." "Haphazard" fails because the work was "painstaking," not careless.
The blank describes how much area the seagrass covers, so "spans" (stretches across) fits. A plant cannot "acknowledge" or "produce" an area.

The first sentence says Johnson's style changed abruptly after 1938. The underlined sentence explains that change: he moved from expressionist landscapes to bold portraits of Black Americans. So it elaborates on that transitional moment. Choice B fails because it is about his change in style, not his travels.

After his employer broke the contract, Israel, a man of "singular patience and mildness," simply looked for another way to make a living. The underlined description implies that his gentle nature is why he accepted the loss instead of fighting for the land. Choice D fails because the point is his mildness, not his bravery.

Tropical species are contrasted with polar and temperate species that are "highly dispersed" across body shapes. So tropical species must be clustered around one form: "concentrated among" deep-bodied shapes. "Habituated to" means accustomed to, which does not describe how a group's body forms are distributed.
By 1830 over 90 percent of Cherokee people could read and write the script, so its use was "widespread." "Infrequent" contradicts that figure.

The text introduces the trend of customized products, explains how companies profit from it, and then notes the difficulty of keeping costs low. That is a trend that both benefits and challenges companies. No single company or contrasting marketing techniques are discussed, so B and D fail.

The text introduces the surprising apparent detection of phosphine on Venus, describes Bains et al.'s modeling of non-biological ways it could form, and then states that if the gas exists, current ideas about Venus's chemistry must be incomplete. That matches C. Choice A fails because the team modeled formation pathways, not flaws in detection methods.

Text 1 claims Carracci (about 1585) was the first Bolognese artist to depict himself painting. Text 2 says Fontana's 1577 self-portrait, which shows an easel in the background, is the earliest Bolognese example of referring to painting. So Text 2's author would point out that Fontana's work came first and also refers to her craft. Choice C is unsupported; nothing says Fontana influenced Carracci.

The researchers are giving a reason why zygomorphic flowers stay open longer: they have fewer potential pollinators, so staying open improves their chances. The longer period could be "attributed to" (explained by) these factors. "Magnified by" would mean the period is enlarged by them, which is less precise than identifying a cause.

After noting that it is hard to watch insects at night, the underlined sentence describes how scientists solved this: time-lapse cameras recording pollinators around the clock. That is a description of their approach. The findings come in later sentences, so D fails.

Wang argues that polling still helps strategists even if predictions fail, so campaigns should not ignore or abandon polling: "neglect." "Supplement" would mean adding to polling, which does not fit "entirely."

Historians dismissed the letters as a hoax because they could not confirm the letters were genuine, so they could not "validate" their authenticity. "Interpret" does not connect to proving whether something is authentic.

The previous sentence says evidence comes partly from freedom seekers' autobiographies, and the underlined sentence gives one: Loguen's account of help from Neshnabé villagers. It is an example. Nothing in the text discusses why Loguen wrote in detail or compares the success of different helpers.

The text opens with a question (why do sand cats purr but lions roar?) and then explains a possible reason involving the hyoid bone. That is a question followed by a possible answer. The explanation is not weakened, so A fails.

The collaboration had tribal citizens working as equal partners in designing and conducting the research, so it is a clear example of the community-based model: it "exemplifies" it. "Circumvents" would mean avoiding the model, the opposite of what happened.
The data had been mostly inaccessible until the project, which now lets a researcher use them. So the project made them "available." The other choices do not contrast with "inaccessible."

Mechanical recycling harms the environment and lowers material quality, and the next sentence presents a better process with "But." So mechanical recycling is seen as "inadequate." "Satisfactory" contradicts the drawbacks listed.

The examples (leaving dead prey, bringing live prey, feeding from the mouth) are all ways predators give food to their young, so they differ in how they "provide" it. The other words do not describe feeding.
Each species has its own repeated series of flashes and pauses, which are "patterns." "Quantities" and "decorations" do not describe a repeated sequence.

Text 1 concludes that lithium and sodium in white dwarf atmospheres point to Earth-like continental crusts. Putirka and Xu argue that such studies overemphasize individual elements and ignore other minerals and non-Earth rock types that could contain them. So they would call the conclusion questionable because it overlooks other possible sources of the elements. Nothing in Text 2 says the conclusion was unexpected or that detecting lithium is unusual.

Kimmerer says the harvesting method lets new plants fill the space, increasing their number and vigor. That means it restores and refills wild populations, or "replenishes" them. "Conditions" is too vague to capture the increase.

The narrator first calls Mr. Verloc "steady like a rock," then immediately adds "a soft kind of rock," softening and limiting that description. So the phrase qualifies the earlier description. Nothing in the passage shows an internal struggle or a private opinion.

De La Cruz's lab combines engineers, biologists, chemists, and physicists and uses insights from all their fields, so his work goes beyond the usual boundaries between disciplines: it is "transcending" them. "Reinforcing" would mean strengthening those boundaries, the opposite.
The sounds can differ depending on ridge spacing, stroke type, and gourd thickness, so they are highly changeable, or "variable." "Powerful" does not relate to the differences described.
The text explains that wave power varies unpredictably, which means it is not steady or "consistent." "Expensive" does not connect to the explanation after the colon.
Alemán loves bold colors from comics, pop art, and Latinx culture, and that passion shows up in her art, so her works are "vivid." "Reserved" would mean muted, the opposite.

The text traces how the Nuyorican Poets Cafe began in Algarín's apartment, moved, expanded, and still supports emerging Nuyorican talent. That is an overview of its founding and mission. Choice C covers only one detail, and the text never explains why the cafe expanded.

The text warns that the effect of posture on cognition should not be overstated and offers O'Brien and Ahmed's study as "a case in point": standing did not change risk-taking as predicted. So it uses the study to show why caution is needed. Choice B fails because the text does not critique the methods of earlier studies.
The poetry is so dense and full of allusions that readers struggle even to identify its subjects, so it is hard to understand, or "comprehend." The other words do not relate to that difficulty.

The water is so clear it is "almost invisible," letting Muir see the plants and fish below, so "clear" means "transparent." "Obvious" and "understandable" are other meanings of clear that do not apply to water.

The underlined statement notes that elephants and caribou keep fixed ranges, which led researchers to guess mammoths did too. The tusk analysis later shows the mammoth's range expanded and then contracted, so that guess was not supported. Choice B fails because the researchers expected mammoths to follow the pattern, not to be an exception to it.

fix.passage: <u>Individual elephants and Arctic herbivores such as caribou tend to have fixed geographic ranges throughout their lifetimes,</u> which had prompted some researchers to speculate that the Arctic woolly mammoth, an extinct elephantid, might have exhibited similar behavior. Mammoth tusks grew in sequential layers, incorporating ingested minerals and organics, and so each ivory stratum reflects the ratio of strontium isotopes (⁸⁷Sr/⁸⁶Sr) in the local environment; thus, the sequence of strata shows where the animal roamed during life. Recent analysis of the strontium ratios in the strata of one Arctic woolly mammoth tusk in relation to the geographic distribution of strontium ratios in the environment shows the animal’s range begin to expand as it reached sexual maturity, only to contract again in its final 1.5 years.

explanation: If retirement transfers are delayed, working adults must support their parents longer, which would hinder their ability to build wealth. "Stymie" means to block or hinder, so it fits. "Compound" would mean increase, the opposite of the effect described.

The speaker first describes a striking sight: a slim black cypress against a gold sky, like a finger pointing up. Then she asks why it is black and why it points upward, wondering what it means. Choice A fails because she does not doubt her description; she questions the meaning of the sight.
The algorithms sorted the recordings "according to type," so the researchers used them to classify, or "categorize," the calls. "Collapse" and "suppress" do not describe sorting.

The blank refers back to "harmless" vibration and warming and contrasts them with a stimulus that "seems less benign." So the word must mean harmless: "innocuous." "Deceptive" adds an idea of trickery the text does not support.

The fossil can help scientists detect and recognize steps in hominid evolution, just as it can "illuminate" the epoch. "Discern" means to perceive or identify, which fits. "Exploit" and "yield" do not describe learning about evolutionary steps.

Star-forming clouds "cannot be touched," but Imara makes 3D-printed models researchers can handle, so the formations need not remain completely untouchable, or "intangible." "Explicable" would mean explainable, which does not connect to touching models.

fix.passage: Stars form in cloudlike swirls of gas and dust that cannot be touched, but astrophysicist Nia Imara believes these formations need not remain completely ______ to researchers: she uses simulation data and sophisticated 3D printers to produce interactive models of these stellar nurseries.

explanation: The underlined sentence summarizes a moment in Mansfield Park where Fanny reads Henry's smile and senses he is reading her. The next sentence says this moment illustrates Butte's concept of "deep intersubjectivity." So it is a synopsis of an interaction that illustrates a concept. Choice A reverses the order: the example comes first, not the claim.

Wauneka "continuously worked" for public health over many years, traveling widely and writing a dictionary, so her effort was "persistent." "Offhand" and "impartial" do not fit the steady dedication described.

The sun has already set, but it is still visible in the streaks of fiery light in the sky. "Manifest" here means able to be seen, or "perceptible." "Dwindling" describes the fading light later in the sentence but is not what "manifest" means.

Text 1 explains that physics at the microscopic level says heat-transfer processes should be reversible, which puzzles physicists. Text 2's experiment confirmed irreversibility at the quantum level, without explaining its cause. The Text 1 author would see this as evidence that the current microscopic understanding is incomplete. Choice C fails because the result conflicts with, rather than fits, the microscopic view.

Pico honors nature's importance in his tribe's beliefs while disliking being in the wilderness himself. Having mixed feelings like this is "ambivalence toward" nature. "Renunciation of" is too strong, since he still honors nature's place in tradition.
Because the fossils are so well preserved, the team has been able to get, or "obtain," detailed information from them. "Hoard" and "reserve" suggest storing something away, not gathering information.

The whole text explains how von Ahn came up with reCAPTCHA and how its first version worked. Scanners and the book project are mentioned only as background to the invention, so B and C are too narrow.

Text 1 says graphic novels rely on images and use language only sparingly. Text 2 argues that the captions and dialogue are essential to understanding the story and can be beautifully written. So Text 2's author would say language matters more in graphic novels than Text 1 admits. Choice D contradicts Text 2's praise of graphic novel writing.
The sentence says Uncle Katsuhisa was "as loud as my father was quiet," directly contrasting the two men. It does not list topics, describe a conversation, or mention meeting new people.
The physicists "closely examine" subatomic particles, so they spend time "inspecting" what is invisible. "Creating" and "deciding" do not describe examining.
The librarian says the poems keep the same "pleasant musical quality" in print as in performance, so they don't lose their "melodic" nature. "Jarring" is the opposite of pleasant and musical.

The crowds, with their wagons, handtrucks, and baskets, are blocking the taxi's way inch by inch, so they are "providing resistance to" its passage. "Arguing about" is the common meaning of dispute but does not fit people physically getting in the way.

The theorists claim earlier diversity strongly shapes later diversity. Cáceres's team stocked pools with very different starting diversity but, contrary to expectations, found little difference after four years. So they would say the view may seem reasonable but their findings do not support it. Choice A fails because their results contradict the view, not just refine it.
